title: Jaw position and horn angle tips tied to Bunk
summary: Blumberg discusses Bill Lofbrower's suggestion about pushing the lower jaw forward as Bunk did, and Bunk holding his horn up.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Lips, teeth and breath: the physical craft of brass playing

blocks.x: I'm gonna just try to sort of jump around on some ideas. I hope it doesn't confuse you too much. But, you know, I'm getting them from Bill's former tape with it. What about Al Hanson? Did he give you any specific tips that he learned from Bunk?

I can't think of any offhand. Uh, thinking about tips from Bunk, though, uh, there was one discussion I got into with Bill Lofbrower, who apparently had been taking some lessons with Bunk, and he suggested, well, he was suggesting for me to, to move my lower jaw out, and I think that he said that Bunk had suggested this to him, or that he had noticed that Bunk was doing this also, uh, business of throwing the lower jaw forward, which, uh, I think Bunk did that to, uh, to a certain extent, when he played.
Did Bill Lofbrower have false teeth too? No.

You know what, maybe that had something to do with it too. No, I don't think it did, no. I mean, it's, uh, I think, uh, a lot of trumpet players have this underbite, uh, uh, and, uh, they play better if they can line up the lower jaw with the upper jaw, as far as the frontal plane is concerned, you know.
Now, I'm trying to think about some, like, uh, you notice some trumpet players, uh, maybe a little undershot, would hold their horn down, and Bunk would hold his very much out front, doesn't he?
Yeah, yeah, well Bunk would hold his up.
And I think, I think he had to push that jaw forward in order to be able to do that.
